claims.claim: Structural construction 447–438 BCE, later sculptural work until about 432 BCE.
Peripteral Doric temple with eight columns on each short side and seventeen on each long side; 46 distinct perimeter columns.
Six-column east and west porch colonnades, 12 additional external Doric columns.
An east/west double cella, noncommunicating ancient compartments; larger eastern chamber and smaller western chamber.
Four tall Ionic supports in the western room and a two-story U-shaped Doric colonnade in the east.
Decorative Ionic frieze around the cella upper walls and inner porches; 115 blocks over roughly 160 metres.
Ninety-two figured metopes across all four exterior faces.
Original building prominently used Pentelic marble.
Raised curved stylobate, column entasis and corner contraction are documented deliberate refinements.
Stylobate 30.88 x 69.50 m and exterior column height about 10.43 m are published summary measurements.
